title: Integrating Expression Data-Based Deep Neural Network Models with Biological Networks to Identify Regulatory Modules for Lung Adenocarcinoma
summary: Deep neural-network analysis of lung adenocarcinoma expression data integrated with biological networks to nominate three candidate regulatory modules involving miR-30a, miR-182 and miR-145. These are computational candidate signatures rather than experimentally established regulatory mechanisms.
ai_technology: Deep neural networks with SHAP feature attribution screened RNA features that were integrated with biological networks to select regulatory modules in lung adenocarcinoma.
organization: University of California, San Francisco; University of California, Los Angeles

source_review.scope: Primary source full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version checked against primary publication metadata.

evidence.tested: The study applied neural-network modeling, SHAP feature attribution and network integration to expression data to identify three candidate modules.
evidence.unknown: The proposed modules are computational hypotheses and are not established causal mechanisms or clinical biomarkers.
